title: CBSE Class 10 Science — Sample Question Paper
subtitle: Science (086) · Theory
subject: Science
instructions: This paper has four sections: A, B, C and D.
Section A contains objective and very short answer questions.
Section B contains case-based questions with data or observation tables.
Internal choices are provided in Section D. Attempt only one option in each such question.
Draw diagrams wherever necessary and label them clearly.

questions.title: Study the graph and answer the questions that follow.

stimulus.title: Average temperature in a city over four weeks
stimulus.altText: Grouped bar chart of maximum and minimum temperatures over four weeks. Maximum falls from 38 to 33 degrees Celsius while minimum falls from 26 to 22 degrees Celsius.

items.prompt: In which week is the difference between the maximum and minimum temperature the greatest?
Calculate the average maximum temperature over the four weeks.
Suggest one reason why the temperature range might be narrower in a coastal city than in an inland city.

questions.title: Read the observations and the graph, then answer the questions.

stimulus.caption: Reaction of metals with copper sulphate solution
rows: Blue solution fades; brown deposit appears

stimulus.title: Temperature of a reaction mixture over time
stimulus.altText: Line chart showing the temperature of a reaction mixture rising from 25 to 43 degrees Celsius over eight minutes and then levelling off.

items.prompt: Which test tubes show a displacement reaction? Explain your answer using the reactivity series.
Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction in test tube B and identify the brown deposit formed in test tube A.
Using the graph, describe how the temperature changes during the reaction. Is the reaction exothermic or endothermic? Justify your answer in 40–60 words.

questions.title: Study the experiment and the chart, then answer the questions.

stimulus.heading: Experiment: electrolysis of water
items: A plastic container is filled with acidified water.
Two carbon electrodes are connected to a 6 V battery.
Test tubes are inverted over each electrode to collect the gases.
The gas collected at the cathode burns with a pop sound.

stimulus.title: Sources of electricity in a state
stimulus.altText: Pie chart of electricity sources: coal 55 percent, hydro 20 percent, solar 15 percent and wind 10 percent.

items.prompt: Name the gases collected at the cathode and the anode during the electrolysis of water, and state the ratio of their volumes.
Using the pie chart, explain one environmental advantage and one limitation of the state's current electricity mix.

questions.title: Read the SWOT analysis and answer the questions.

stimulus.title: Adoption of rooftop solar power in a city

items.prompt: Using the SWOT analysis, suggest two practical steps a city could take to increase rooftop solar adoption.
Explain why solar energy is considered a renewable source while coal is not.
